main_text.p: Quarto, Tunica palati duritie munita, inter quam & linguam cibi volutati magis attenuantur.

Deglutionis membrum est Gula seu Oesophagus, qui est membraneus, nerveus & exanguis canalis, à faucibus ad ventriculum usque continuè porrectus, via nimirum deglutionis, per quam cibus ex ore masticatus in ventriculū descendit.Oesophagus seu Gula.
Ut commodior esset deglutio, substantia gulæ modò extendi, modò concidere potest, in principio quidem densior, quàm in ventre.
Deglutioni ferunt suppetias primùm fibræ tunicæ exterioris latæ seu transversæ, quæ expellunt in ventrem.Deglutio quomodo fiat.
Secundò, quatuor Musculi Faucium, & duo, qui è pectore fursum ducuntur ad gulam, ad alimentum deducendum de-orsum.
Tertiò, Motus Epiglottidis, quæ tempore ingestionis ascendit, & gulæ tunc descendenti locum præbet, simulque aspe-ram arteriam obturat, ne à cibo deviante molestetur.
Organa egestionis sunt vasa chylum-Organa e-gestionis.

page.notes: The first paragraph is a list item ("Quarto") and does not continue from the previous page. The last line ends in a printed hyphen at "chylum-"; the rest of that line is hidden by show-through and could not be read. "furfum" and "deorsum" are read with the long s as plain s ("fursum", "de-orsum") as the rule requires; the spelling of the scan is uncertain. Faint show-through from the reverse side appears in the right margin and between the lines and is not transcribed. Marginal notes are placed at the paragraphs they stand beside.
